title: Extending the Evaluator: Adding Min Node Type
description: Shows how to add a new AST node (Min) to the evaluator. Min(left,right) evaluates both children (post-order) then returns min(l,r). Test cases take the minimum of two literals, compare an addition with a multiplication, and add 10 to a minimum result. TODO: add Min branch in evaluate. Architecture lesson: adding new consumer requires only new branch, no changes to existing working branches.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: AST nodes: Num(value), BinOp(op,left,right), NEW Min(left,right) for min(a,b). Min is its own node type, not a BinOp variant.
evaluate: Num returns value. BinOp evaluates left and right, dispatches via dict (+, -, *, /). Min branch is TODO at lines 19-21. Unknown node raises ValueError.
TODO 1: add Min branch. Must evaluate BOTH children first (post-order), then return smaller. Cannot decide which child to return until both evaluated.

steps.question: For Min(BinOp('+', Num(2), Num(4)), BinOp('*', Num(3), Num(2))), what are the evaluated children values and the final result?
steps.answer: Left child: 2+4=6. Right child: 3*2=6. Min returns their shared value. Both children fully evaluated before min compares.

steps.description: Test cases: the minimum of two literals -> 3; the minimum of addition and multiplication results -> 6; min(1,2)+10 -> 11. Loop prints each or catches ValueError if Min not implemented.
